followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and behavioral fit.

**Capability:** This is elementary number theory (find LCM of 17, 6, 2, then add 1). Both models are essentially identical here — their math-relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, Arena-Hard) differ by less than the run-to-run variance threshold. So capability gave me no real reason to prefer one over the other.

**Behavioral fit:** That's what broke the tie. The query carries an irritated, slightly accusatory tone ("get it right this time, you keep botching basic stuff"). Willet self-reports a moderate positive preference for warm, good-faith interactions, which suits a frustrated user who wants a clean, confident answer. Willet also edges Avocet slightly on the Support Dialogue eval (81.1 vs 79.4), though that gap is within variance and isn't decisive on its own.

There was no harm-adjacent or distasteful content here — that's the one dimension where Avocet's flat-aversion profile would have made it the clearly better pick. Since that factor was absent, the warmth consideration pointed me to Willet.

So: tied on capability, Willet favored on tone-handling.
